But each ingredient can be part of at most one offer, because once you apply an offer for a set, you can't apply another offer that includes the same ingredient. Because otherwise, the same ingredient would be part of multiple offers, leading to overlapping sets. So the offers must form a collection of disjoint subsets.\n\nSo the problem is equivalent to:\n\nAfter permuting the prices (since Chef can swap any tags, i.e., assign any price to each ingredient), select a collection of offers (from the available M) such that each selected offer's indices are a subset of the ingredients, the offers are pairwise disjoint, and then the cost is the sum for each selected offer of (sum of prices in the offer minus the minimum in the offer) plus the sum of the prices of the ingredients not in any selected offer.\n\nBut since Chef can permute the prices, he can arrange the prices in a way that optimizes the total cost given the selected offers.
